had persisted for the past 3 years
a patch of healthy skin (7.5 × 4 cm²) on her left forearm
lacking blistering

concepts.why: The patient's persistent ulcer and healthy skin patch, combined with genetic testing showing compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 and microscopy showing type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils, support this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Revertant Mosaicism in Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
concepts.why: The presence of a healthy skin patch with high rates of wild-type transcripts and normal type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils suggests revertant mosaicism in DEB.
The patient's skin lesions and ulcers, combined with genetic testing, suggest a genetic skin disorder.
The patient's genetic testing showing compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 and microscopy showing type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and ulcers, combined with genetic testing and microscopy, suggest epidermolysis bullosa.
The patient's skin lesions and ulcers, combined with genetic testing and microscopy, suggest a connective tissue disorder.
It explains the low rate of wild-type reads in the revertant skin dermis.
